## Epic 1: Table Layout Improvements

The core data surfaces (positions, dividends/deposits, global universe, screener) render through a single shared `dms-base-table` component. After this Epic, every table in the app renders with the standard Angular Material `mat-table` / `matColumnDef` / `mat-header-row` / `mat-row` syntax instead of the bespoke two-region DIV layout, and the header/table separation (which was only there to work around sticky-header scroll bugs) is removed. Users get the same 57px rows, virtual scroll, multi-column sort with rank badges, selection, and inline-edit cells — but built on the standard, more maintainable Material table primitives that were the original implementation.

**ADs covered:** AD-1, AD-2, AD-4
**FRs covered:** FR-2, FR-3, FR-4, FR-5, FR-7

### Story 1.1: Unit tests for the mat-table base-table conversion

As a developer,
I want a red-phase unit-test scaffold for the `dms-base-table` conversion to `mat-table`,
So that the implementation story has a defined, executable contract to make pass.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the `dms-base-table` component is rendered in the Angular test harness
**When** the unit-test suite for `base-table.component.spec.ts` runs
**Then** it asserts the template emits `<mat-table>`, `<ng-container matColumnDef>`, `<mat-header-cell *matHeaderCellDef>`, and `<mat-cell *matCellDef>` markup
**And** it asserts the old two-region DIV markers (`.dms-table-header` / `.dms-outer-scroller` / `cdk-virtual-scroll-viewport` body) are no longer required for the header/body split
**And** it asserts sorting, selection, `renderedRangeChange`, and default cell rendering still behave as before

### Story 1.2: Convert dms-base-table to Angular Material mat-table

As a developer,
I want `dms-base-table` rebuilt on `mat-table` / `matColumnDef` / `mat-header-row` / `mat-row`,
So that the table layout is standard, the sticky-header bugs disappear, and the header/table separation is removed.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the current `apps/dms-material/src/app/shared/components/base-table/base-table.component.html` uses the DIV two-region layout
**When** it is converted to the Material `mat-table` syntax
**Then** the header and body render as a single standard table without the `dms-outer-scroller` / header-viewport separation
**And** the original table-based implementation at <https://github.com/DaveMBush/dms-workspace/commit/36ee7e7cb9910d9ac54cb2c719ffd36cef649520> is used as the reference for the starting point
**And** the 57px row height, virtual scroll, multi-column MatSort with rank badges, SelectionModel + mat-checkbox, and default cell rendering are preserved
**And** every consumer of `dms-base-table` (dividend-deposits, open-positions, sold-positions, global-universe, global-screener) still renders correctly

### Story 1.3: e2e test for the mat-table table layout

As a user,
I want the data tables to render and interact correctly after the conversion,
So that I can sort, select, scroll, and inline-edit in every table surface without regressions.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the app is running and a table surface (e.g. open-positions or global-universe) is loaded
**When** the Playwright e2e suite drives the table
**Then** rows render with the Material table markup and the 57px row height
**And** clicking a sortable header toggles sort direction and shows the rank badge
**And** the select-all checkbox and per-row checkboxes toggle selection
**And** vertical scrolling renders rows (virtual scroll) without breaking layout
**And** inline edit of a cell commits on Enter and cancels on Escape

## Epic 2: Remove Return of Capital

Return of Capital was previously modeled as a deposit type separate from Dividend, but the app only tracks total income generated by the investments regardless of its source. After this Epic, Return of Capital is no longer a distinct deposit type anywhere in the application — it is consolidated under Dividend — so the `divDepositTypes` seeding, the data-model documentation, and any residual handling are reduced to the canonical Dividend / Deposit type set. Users see one coherent income model with no stray "Return of Capital" option or record.

**ADs covered:** AD-7, AD-1
**FRs covered:** FR-5, FR-6, FR-7

### Story 2.1: Unit tests for removing Return of Capital

As a developer,
I want a red-phase unit-test scaffold asserting the `divDepositTypes` seeding no longer emits a "Return of Capital" type,
So that the implementation story has a defined contract to make pass.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the Postgres seed routine `seedDivDepositTypes` in `scripts/seed-postgres.ts`
**When** the seed is executed against a clean database
**Then** the `divDepositType` rows seeded contain no "Return of Capital" entry
**And** the canonical server seed (`get-top-div-deposit-types.function.ts`) continues to seed exactly Dividend + Deposit

### Story 2.2: Remove Return of Capital handling

As a developer,
I want every separate handling of "Return of Capital" removed and consolidated under Dividend,
So that the app models a single income concept per the PRD glossary and AD-7.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** `scripts/seed-postgres.ts:97` seeds `{ name: 'Return of Capital' }` and `docs/data-models.md:222` lists "Return of Capital" as an example type
**When** the Return-of-Capital references are removed
**Then** the Postgres seed no longer creates a "Return of Capital" `divDepositType`
**And** the `docs/data-models.md` deposit-type example no longer lists "Return of Capital"
**And** no remaining code path, spec, or UI string treats Return of Capital as a distinct deposit type

## Epic 3: Table Layout Improvements — div-based mat-table conversion

Epic 1 converted `dms-base-table` to `<table mat-table>` (native table element + Material directive) but kept native sticky headers, and existing unit/e2e tests that asserted the native `<table>`/`<tr>`/`<td>` markup forced it back away from divs. This Epic completes the conversion to Material's **div-based** custom-element syntax (`<mat-table>`, `<mat-header-cell>`, `<mat-cell>`, `<mat-row>`) so the table renders as a single standard `mat-table` of `<div>`s with natively sticky headers — removing the native-table sticky-header quirks and any residual two-region workaround. The existing tests that assert the old native markup are updated (or skipped) to target the div-based format, so they no longer force the implementation back to tables.

**ADs covered:** AD-4
**FRs covered:** FR-2, FR-3, FR-4, FR-5, FR-7

### Story 3.1: Unit tests for the div-based mat-table conversion

As a developer,
I want red-phase unit-test assertions that `BaseTableComponent` renders Material's **div-based** `<mat-table>` markup (no native `<table>`/`<th>`/`<td>`/`<tr>` elements) while preserving the load-bearing `.dms-*` classes, ARIA roles, and `data-column` attributes,
So that Story 3.2 has a defined contract to make pass when it converts the template from Epic 1's `<table mat-table>` element form to the div-based custom-element syntax.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the `BaseTableComponent` is rendered in the Angular test harness with Epic 1's `<table mat-table>` template
**When** the unit-test suite for `base-table-mat-table.spec.ts` runs
**Then** it asserts a div-based Material table (`mat-table[role="table"]` / `.mat-mdc-table`) exists inside the viewport and that native `table`/`th`/`td`/`tr` elements are absent from the component DOM
**And** it asserts the load-bearing selectors survive: `.dms-header-cell[role="columnheader"][data-column]`, `.dms-body-row[role="row"]`, `.dms-body-cell[data-column]`
**And** it asserts the column-header row computes to a sticky position so it pins above the viewport body
**And** every div-based assertion is marked `it.skip` (red-phase by skip) while the existing class/role/data-column assertions stay unskipped and green

### Story 3.2: Convert DMS BaseTable to div-based mat-table

As a developer,
I want `BaseTableComponent`'s template converted from Epic 1's `<table mat-table>` element form (native `<table>`/`<th>`/`<td>`/`<tr>`) to Material's **div-based** custom-element syntax (`<mat-table>`, `<mat-header-cell>`, `<mat-cell>`, `<mat-row>`),
So that the table renders as a single standard `mat-table` of `<div>`s with natively sticky headers — removing the native-table sticky-header quirks and any residual two-region workaround — while every load-bearing `.dms-*` class, ARIA role, `data-column` attribute, and event binding is preserved so existing unit tests and ~50 consumer e2e specs keep passing.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the current `apps/dms-material/src/app/shared/components/base-table/base-table.component.html` uses `<table mat-table>` with native `<th>`/`<td>`/`<tr>` elements
**When** it is converted to the div-based Material syntax (`<mat-table>`, `<mat-header-cell>`, `<mat-cell>`, `<mat-row>`)
**Then** no native `<table>`/`<th>`/`<td>`/`<tr>` elements remain in the template and every attribute, binding, class, event, `data-column`, and ARIA role is preserved exactly
**And** Material's host-bound roles (`role="columnheader"`, `role="row"`) are intact on the div-based elements so `.dms-header-cell[role="columnheader"]` / `.dms-body-row[role="row"]` still resolve
**And** the SCSS native-element selector (`.dms-table-body table.mat-mdc-table`) is updated to target `<mat-table>` and any residual two-region sticky CSS is removed — Material's native sticky headers own pinning
**And** Story 3.1's red-phase unit assertions are unskipped and green, and the project builds cleanly

### Story 3.3: E2E test for the div-based mat-table layout

As a user,
I want the data tables to render and interact correctly after the **div-based** `mat-table` conversion (Story 3.2),
So that I can sort, select, scroll, and inline-edit in every table surface without regressions — with a fresh e2e spec proving the div-based layout works end-to-end, and the handful of consumer specs that still target native `<table>`/`<tr>`/`<td>` selectors updated to the new markup.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the app is running and a table surface (open-positions or global-universe) is loaded with seeded data
**When** the Playwright e2e suite drives the div-based table
**Then** the `.mat-mdc-table` container renders inside the viewport with NO native `<table>` element, body rows are `[role="row"].dms-body-row`, and header cells are `[role="columnheader"].dms-header-cell`
**And** scrolling keeps the column-header row pinned above the body (Material's native sticky headers) while virtual scroll renders additional rows
**And** sorting toggles direction with the rank badge, and selection toggles row state
**And** the four consumer specs that still target native-table selectors (`open-positions`, `symbol-filter-header`, `base-table-layout-regression` header selector, `universe-table-workflows`) are updated to div-based equivalents, while the ~50 class/role-based consumer specs and the `dms-base-table` host-selector specs pass unchanged

## Epic 4: Fix add-position / add-div-deposit navigation crash (SmartNgRX state corruption)

After this Epic, adding a new position on the Open Positions screen or adding a dividend/deposit on the Dividend Deposits screen no longer corrupts in-memory state: navigating to Sold Positions, Dividend Deposits, or any other route after an add renders normally with no exception, and the added row appears correctly in its table and persists across a page reload. The root cause is that SmartNgRX's `SmartArray.add()` → `addToStore()` reconstructs the parent Account entity's virtual-array field (`openTrades` / `divDeposits`) as `{ indexes, length }` only — dropping `startIndex` — so any later read of that virtual array (e.g. a computed signal re-evaluated on route change) throws.

**ADs covered:** AD-2
**FRs covered:** FR-2, FR-3, FR-5, FR-7

### Story 4.1: Unit tests for add-position / add-div-deposit SmartNgRX state integrity (red-phase)

As a developer,
I want red-phase unit-test assertions that the parent `Account` entity's virtual-array field (`openTrades` / `divDeposits`) retains all three properties — `startIndex`, `indexes`, and `length` — after calling SmartNgRX's `SmartArray.add()`,
So that Story 4.2 has a defined, executable contract to make pass when it fixes the state corruption in the add-position and add-div-deposit flows.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the `AddPositionService.createDialogCloseHandler(...)` path processes a valid dialog result against an account with existing open trades
**When** the post-add unit test reads the parent `Account` entity's `openTrades` field from the SmartNgRX store
**Then** `startIndex` is a number (not `undefined`), `indexes` is an array whose last element equals the new trade's id, and `length` equals the prior length + 1
**And** the parallel assertion set for `DividendDepositsComponentService.addDivDeposit(...)` verifies the parent `Account` entity's `divDeposits` field has all three properties defined with the same invariants

**Given** an add (position or dividend deposit) has completed in the unit test
**When** the computed signal that reads the virtual array is re-evaluated (`OpenPositionsComponentService.selectOpenPositions()` for trades; `DividendDepositsComponentService.dividends()` for deposits)
**Then** it does not throw — iterating every valid index returns a row object or string placeholder id, never an exception from a missing/undefined `startIndex`

**Given** the red-phase assertions above are written into the spec files
**When** `nx test dms-material` runs immediately after this story
**Then** all new assertions are marked `.skip()` (`it.skip`) so CI stays green while the bug still exists, and every pre-existing test in `open-positions-component.service.spec.ts` and `dividend-deposits-component.service.spec.ts` remains unskipped and green

### Story 4.2: Fix add-position / add-div-deposit SmartNgRX virtual-array state corruption

As a user (Dave),
I want adding a position or dividend deposit to not corrupt the in-memory `Account` entity's virtual-array state,
So that navigating away from the screen after an add does not throw an exception and my data is accurate and durable.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** SmartNgRX's `BaseArrayProxy.addToStore()` reconstructs the parent virtual-array field as `{ indexes, length }` only — omitting `startIndex` (verified in installed `@smarttools/smart-core`)
**When** the fix is applied at the lowest correct layer so that after `.add()`, the parent Account entity's `openTrades` / `divDeposits` retains all three properties: `startIndex` (a number), `indexes` (array with the new id appended), and `length` (prior + 1)
**Then** no property is dropped or set to `undefined` for either add path

**Given** Story 4.1's red-phase unit assertions are unskipped
**When** `nx test dms-material` runs after the fix
**Then** all of Story 4.1's state-integrity and no-throw assertions pass, and no pre-existing test regresses

**Given** an add completes (HTTP round-trip + store reconciliation) in the running app
**When** the user navigates away from Open Positions or Dividend Deposits to another route
**Then** no exception is thrown and the view renders normally — verified by unit-level no-throw assertions; the e2e verification of this behavior belongs to Story 4.3

### Story 4.3: E2E test for add-position / add-div-deposit then navigate

As a user (Dave),
I want an end-to-end proof that adding a position or dividend deposit and then navigating away does not crash the app,
So that I can trust both add flows in real use — including persistence of the added row.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the app is running with seeded data and an account panel is open on the Open Positions screen
**When** a position is added via the Add Position dialog and the user navigates to Sold Positions (or Dividend Deposits)
**Then** zero `pageerror` events and zero `console.error` events are captured for the whole flow, and the target route renders its table normally

**Given** the app is running with seeded data and an account panel is open on the Dividend Deposits screen
**When** a dividend deposit is added and the user navigates to Open Positions (or Sold Positions)
**Then** zero `pageerror` events and zero `console.error` events are captured for the whole flow, and the target route renders its table normally

**Given** an add has completed in either flow
**When** the page is reloaded (`page.reload()`)
**Then** the added row is still present with correct data (symbol, quantity, price, date for positions; date, amount, type for deposits) — server round-trip confirmed
**And** the existing e2e specs `open-positions.spec.ts` and `dividend-deposits-modal.spec.ts` pass unchanged alongside the new spec

## Epic 5: Column Headers — wrap + top alignment (no clipping)

Every table in the app renders through the single shared `dms-base-table` component, whose `.dms-header-cell` style currently clips header text with `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap`. After this Epic, column headers show their full text — wrapping onto multiple lines instead of being cut off — and start at the top of the header cell. Body cells are intentionally left unchanged (single-line, truncated) so the fixed 57px row height and CDK virtual-scroll itemSize stay stable.

### Story 5.1: Unit tests for column header wrap + top alignment (red-phase)

As a developer,
I want a red-phase unit-test scaffold asserting that `dms-base-table` column headers wrap fully (no clipping) and align to the top of their cell,
So that Story 5.2 has a defined, executable contract to make pass when it removes the header text-clipping styles.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** `dms-base-table` renders a column whose `header` is long enough to wrap at the configured column width
**When** the rendered `.dms-header-cell` computed style is inspected
**Then** it does NOT clip: `white-space` resolves to `normal`/unset (not `nowrap`) and `text-overflow` is not `ellipsis`
**And** a wrapped header cell's text starts at the top of the cell (computed `vertical-align: top`, or an equivalent top-alignment assertion)

**Given** a short single-line header
**When** it renders with the same non-clipping, top-aligned style
**Then** there is no regression to single-line headers

### Story 5.2: Remove column header clipping; allow wrap + top alignment

As a user (Dave),
I want the column headers in every table to show their full text — wrapping onto multiple lines instead of being cut off — and to start at the top of the header cell,
So that no header information is hidden by `white-space: nowrap` / `text-overflow: ellipsis` styling.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the shared `.dms-header-cell` block in `apps/dms-material/src/app/shared/components/base-table/base-table.component.scss` (lines 49–67) currently sets `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap`
**When** those three clipping declarations are removed and `vertical-align: top` is added to the same block
**Then** a wrapped header cell shows its full text, aligned to the top of the cell

**Given** the `.dms-body-cell` block (lines 112–117) sets `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap` and the fixed `--mat-table-row-item-container-height: 57px` row height (line 10)
**When** Story 5.2's change is applied
**Then** body cells are untouched — data rows keep their single-line, 57px behavior and virtual-scroll itemSize stays stable

**Given** Story 5.1's red-phase unit assertions
**When** they are unskipped and `nx test dms-material` runs
**Then** all pass (green) with no pre-existing regression in `base-table.component.spec.ts`

### Story 5.3: E2E test for column header wrap + top alignment

As a user (Dave),
I want an end-to-end proof that every table's column headers show their full text — wrapping onto multiple lines instead of being clipped — and start at the top of the header cell, across different screen sizes,
So that I can trust no header information is hidden by styling in real use.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** a table view with long column headers (e.g., Open Positions or Universe) rendered through `dms-base-table`
**When** each `.dms-header-cell` is inspected at two viewport sizes (desktop + tablet)
**Then** the cell shows its full text (scroll height equals client height, no ellipsis, computed `white-space` not `nowrap`) and the first line of header text sits at the top edge of the cell bounding box

**Given** the existing e2e specs `open-positions.spec.ts` and `dividend-deposits-modal.spec.ts`
**When** they run alongside the new spec on chromium
**Then** all pass unchanged — no pre-existing test regresses

## Epic 6: Remove PrimeNg

The app's UI is built entirely on Angular Material; there are zero real PrimeNg references in dms-material source (no TS import, no SCSS `@import`/`@use`). The only traces are two stale package declarations (`@primeng/themes`, `primeng`) in the workspace-root `package.json` (dms-material has no per-app manifest — deps are root-hoisted) and a misleading comment at line 1 of `apps/dms-material/src/themes/_theme-variables.scss`. After this Epic, both packages are removed from the dependency set with no remaining references anywhere.

### Story 6.1: Unit tests asserting no PrimeNg references remain (red-phase)

As a developer,
I want a red-phase test that fails while `@primeng/themes` and `primeng` are still declared in the dms-material dependency set or referenced in source,
So that Story 6.2 has an executable contract proving PrimeNg is fully removed before the packages are deleted.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the workspace-root `package.json` currently declares both `@primeng/themes` and `primeng` under `dependencies` (dms-material has no per-app manifest — deps are root-hoisted)
**When** a new test reads that manifest
**Then** it asserts neither key is present — failing (red) while the deps still exist

**Given** the dms-material source tree (`apps/dms-material/src/**/*.{ts,scss}`)
**When** a sibling test scans every file for an import of `primeng`, `@primeng/themes`, or any `@primeng/*` specifier
**Then** it asserts zero references (this already holds — the only trace is a comment, not an import)

### Story 6.2: Remove PrimeNg packages from dms-material

As a user (Dave),
I want the `@primeng/themes` and `primeng` packages removed from dms-material with no remaining references in source,
So that the app depends only on Angular Material for its UI components.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** both PrimeNg keys are declared in the workspace-root `package.json` under `dependencies` (dms-material has no per-app manifest — deps are root-hoisted) and a stale comment sits at line 1 of `apps/dms-material/src/themes/_theme-variables.scss`
**When** the two dependency entries are deleted, `pnpm install` runs, and the comment is removed
**Then** neither package appears in the manifest or `node_modules`, no source file imports any `@primeng/*` specifier, and a case-insensitive grep of `apps/dms-material/src` for `primeng` returns zero hits

**Given** Story 6.1's red-phase tests are unskipped
**When** `nx test dms-material`, `nx run dms-material:lint`, and the build target run
**Then** all pass (green) with no new errors — removal is safe because `styles.scss` uses only `@angular/material` + local theme files

## Epic 7: Yahoo-Finance2 → 4.0.4

The server's single raw import of `yahoo-finance2` lives in `apps/server/src/app/routes/settings/yahoo-finance.instance.ts`, which re-exports a `yahooFinance` instance consumed by three call sites (`search()` ×2, `quote()` ×1). The package is declared on the v3 line (`^3.13.0`) in the root `package.json`. After this Epic it targets 4.0.4, any v3→v4 API breakage is fixed at that one import point (or the call sites), and consumer tests stay insulated from the package internals by mocking the instance module rather than importing the raw package.

### Story 7.1: Unit tests for yahoo-finance2 v4 upgrade contract (red-phase)

As a developer,
I want a red-phase test that fails while `yahoo-finance2` is still on the v3 line and asserts the declared version targets 4.0.4 with consumer tests mocking the instance module rather than importing the raw package,
So that Story 7.2 has an executable contract proving the upgrade landed without coupling any test to the package's internal implementation.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** `yahoo-finance2` is declared in the root `package.json` (line 69) as `"^3.13.0"`
**When** a new test reads that manifest value
**Then** it asserts the version satisfies `^4.0.4` — failing (red) while on v3

**Given** the consumer specs (`resolve-cusip.function.spec.ts`, `get-last-price.function.spec.ts`) already mock the instance module `settings/yahoo-finance.instance.ts`
**When** a sibling test inspects them
**Then** it asserts they do NOT import the raw `yahoo-finance2` specifier — locking in the "mock the instance module" contract so tests survive future package swaps

### Story 7.2: Upgrade yahoo-finance2 to v4

As a user (Dave),
I want the `yahoo-finance2` package upgraded from the v3 line to version 4.0.4, with any resulting API breakage fixed at the single import point and consumer tests insulated from the package internals,
So that the server runs on the current major release of the library.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** `yahoo-finance2` is declared in the root `package.json` (line 69) as `"^3.13.0"` and only `settings/yahoo-finance.instance.ts` imports the raw package
**When** the declaration is bumped to target 4.0.4, `pnpm install` runs, and any v3→v4 constructor/option or method-signature changes are fixed at that import point (or the three call sites)
**Then** the exported `yahooFinance` instance still works — all three consumers (`search()` in `symbol/search/index.ts` + `import/resolve-cusip.function.ts`, `quote()` in `settings/common/get-last-price.function.ts`) compile and pass their existing unit tests

**Given** Story 7.1's red-phase tests are unskipped
**When** the server test runner, `nx run dms-server:lint`, and the build target run
**Then** all pass (green) with no pre-existing regression — the version assertion is now green

> Note: the epic prose says this "will need to be done in one story," but the validator forbids a single-story epic (count must satisfy both `% 2` and `% 3`). This is therefore the minimal valid pair: a red-phase contract + its implementation, with no e2e story.

## Epic 8: Right Align Numbers

Every table in the app renders through the single shared `dms-base-table` component, whose body cells currently inherit default left alignment — so numbers (quantities, prices, yields, gains) sit at the left edge of their column and do not line up for comparison. After this Epic, every numeric column (`type: 'number' | 'currency'`) is right-aligned in its cell across all table surfaces (global-universe, global-screener, open-positions, sold-positions, dividend-deposits), achieved centrally in `dms-base-table` so no per-table template changes are required.

### Story 8.1: Unit tests for numeric column right-alignment in dms-base-table

As a developer,
I want a red-phase unit-test scaffold asserting that `dms-base-table` body cells for numeric columns (`type: 'number' | 'currency'`) are right-aligned while non-numeric columns stay left-aligned,
So that Story 8.2 has a defined, executable contract to make pass when it adds the type-derived alignment class and CSS.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** `BaseTableComponent` is rendered with a column set containing at least one `type: 'number'` column (e.g. `{ field: 'qty', header: 'Qty', type: 'number' }`) and one `type: 'currency'` column, plus a `type: 'text'`/default column and a `type: 'date'` column
**When** the rendered body cells are inspected

## Epic 9: Consistent Date Format

Table date columns are rendered by two different code paths that disagree on format. The shared `dms-base-table` default cell and the open-positions custom template both use the locale-dependent `'shortDate'` pipe (which under en-US renders `M/d/yy`, e.g. `7/14/26`), while dividend-deposits and global-universe already render an explicit `'MM/dd/yyyy'`. After this Epic, every table date column — Open Positions Ex-Date / Buy Date / Sell Date and Sold Positions Buy Date / Sell Date — renders as `MM/DD/YYYY`, independent of the active locale.

### Story 9.1: Unit tests for consistent MM/DD/YYYY date format in tables

As a developer,
I want a red-phase unit-test scaffold asserting that every table date column renders as `MM/DD/YYYY`,
So that Story 9.2 has a defined, executable contract to make pass when it replaces the remaining locale-dependent `shortDate` usages with an explicit `'MM/dd/yyyy'` format.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** `BaseTableComponent` is rendered with a `type: 'date'` column and a known date value
**When** the rendered body cell text is inspected
**Then** it matches the `MM/DD/YYYY` pattern (e.g. `07/14/2026`) — NOT the locale-dependent `shortDate` form (`M/d/yy`, e.g. `7/14/26`)

**Given** `OpenPositionsComponent` is rendered with a row whose `exDate` is set
**When** the Ex-Date cell text is inspected
**Then** it matches `MM/DD/YYYY`

**Given** the red-phase assertions above are written into the spec files
**When** `nx test dms-material` runs immediately after this story
**Then** all new assertions are marked `.skip()` (`it.skip`) so CI stays green while the format is not yet standardized, and every pre-existing test remains unskipped and green

### Story 9.2: Standardize table date format to MM/DD/YYYY

As a user (Dave),
I want every date column in the tables to be formatted as `MM/DD/YYYY`,
So that dates are consistent across all screens and not dependent on the browser/system locale.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the shared default-cell date case at `apps/dms-material/src/app/shared/components/base-table/base-table.component.html:150` uses `date: 'shortDate'`
**When** it is changed to `date: 'MM/dd/yyyy'`
**Then** any table that uses the default cell renderer (Sold Positions Buy Date / Sell Date) renders `MM/DD/YYYY`

**Given** the open-positions custom `#cellTemplate` date case in `apps/dms-material/src/app/account-panel/open-positions/open-positions.component.html` uses `date : 'shortDate'`
**When** it is changed to `date: 'MM/dd/yyyy'`
**Then** Open Positions Ex-Date / Buy Date / Sell Date render `MM/DD/YYYY`

**Given** dividend-deposits and global-universe already use `'MM/dd/yyyy'`, and the auth profile cards use a non-table `date: 'medium'` surface
**When** Story 9.2's two changes are applied
**Then** those surfaces are untouched — only the two `shortDate` table sites change

**Given** Story 9.1's red-phase unit assertions are unskipped
**When** `nx test dms-material` runs after the change
**Then** all pass (green) with no pre-existing regression

### Story 9.3: E2E test for consistent MM/DD/YYYY date format

As a user (Dave),
I want an end-to-end proof that table dates render as `MM/DD/YYYY`,
So that I can trust the format is consistent in real use on the screens where it was previously wrong.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** Sold Positions is loaded with seeded data
**When** the Buy Date and Sell Date cell text for a sampled row is read
**Then** both match the `MM/DD/YYYY` pattern (`/^\d{2}\/\d{2}\/\d{4}$/`) — not the short `M/d/yy` form

**Given** Open Positions is loaded with seeded data

**Then** it matches the same `MM/DD/YYYY` pattern

## Epic 11: Electron Session Persistence (Cookies + LocalStorage)

In the web app, I'm currently saving/storing cookies for things like sorting, filtering, and login, that aren't persisting once I've exited the electron application. Some don't seem to be saving at all. We need to find some way to ensure cookies are properly saved and retrieved within the electron environment.

After this Epic, state the user sets in the Electron app — sort/filter preferences (localStorage), theme, remember-me, and the Cognito auth cookie — survives an application exit and re-launch. The root cause is that `apps/electron/src/main.ts` resolves a **random** port on every launch via `findAvailablePort()` (`main.ts:289`) and then loads `http://localhost:${port}` (`main.ts:207`); because cookies and localStorage are scoped to the origin, a new port each launch is a new origin, so all previously-saved state is discarded. Pinning the app to a **stable default origin** (a fixed default port) makes the origin constant across launches so saved cookies and localStorage persist; the existing `DMS_SMOKE_PORT` override for smoke tests is preserved unchanged.

**ADs covered:** AD-5, AD-10
**FRs covered:** FR-19

### Story 11.1: Unit tests for a stable Electron origin across launches (red-phase)

As a developer,
I want a red-phase unit-test scaffold asserting that the Electron main process resolves to a fixed default port (and therefore a stable `http://localhost:<port>` origin) on every launch when no override is set,
So that Story 11.2 has a defined, executable contract to make pass when it replaces the random-port resolution with a stable one.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** `apps/electron/src/main.ts` currently resolves its port via `findAvailablePort()` (`main.ts:289`)
**When** a unit test exercises the port-resolution logic with no `DMS_SMOKE_PORT` set
**Then** it asserts the resolved port equals a single fixed default constant (not a random value) — failing (red) while `findAvailablePort()` is still used

**Given** the port-resolution logic is invoked twice in succession with no override
**When** both resolutions are compared
**Then** they return the identical port, proving the origin `http://localhost:<port>` is stable across launches so cookies and localStorage persist — failing (red) while a random port is chosen each time

**Given** `DMS_SMOKE_PORT` is set to a valid value in the environment
**When** the port-resolution logic runs
**Then** it returns that override value, preserving existing smoke-test behavior (`parseSmokePort`, `main.ts:232`) — this assertion passes today and must remain green

**Given** the red-phase assertions above are written into the spec files
**When** `nx test electron` runs immediately after this story
**Then** all new assertions are marked `.skip()` (`it.skip`) so CI stays green while a random port is still chosen, and every pre-existing Electron spec remains unskipped and green

### Story 11.2: Pin the Electron app to a stable default origin (fixed port)

As a user (Dave),
I want my sort/filter preferences, theme, remember-me choice, and login session to still be there when I reopen the desktop app,
So that I don't have to re-authenticate and re-configure every time I relaunch.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** `apps/electron/src/main.ts` resolves its port at startup (`main.ts:285-290`) by calling `findAvailablePort()` when no override is set
**When** that resolution is changed to use a fixed default port constant (e.g. `7420`, which collides with none of the ports already in use — 3000, 4200, 4566, 8080) instead of a random one
**Then** every launch loads the same origin `http://localhost:<fixed-port>`, so cookies (AD-5 auth cookie) and localStorage (sort/filter/theme/remember-me) are saved to and retrieved from the same origin across launches

**Given** the fixed default port is already in use by another process at startup
**When** the app attempts to bind it
**Then** it falls back to `findAvailablePort()` for that launch only, so the app still starts (a degraded but non-crashing path) rather than failing to launch

**Given** `DMS_SMOKE_PORT` is set in the environment
**When** the app resolves its port
**Then** it uses that override exactly as before (`parseSmokePort`, `main.ts:232`) — smoke-test behavior is unchanged

**Given** Story 11.1's red-phase unit assertions are unskipped
**When** `nx test electron` runs after the change
**Then** all pass (green) with no pre-existing regression in the Electron specs, and the CSP (`configureContentSecurityPolicy`) and navigation guards that read `port` continue to work against the fixed origin

### Story 11.3: E2E test for cookie + localStorage persistence across an app relaunch

As a user (Dave),
I want end-to-end proof that my saved state survives quitting and reopening the desktop app,
So that I can trust login and preferences persist in real use, not just in unit tests.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

**Given** the Electron app is launched via Playwright's `_electron` harness (the pattern already used by `apps/electron/src/electron-package-launch.smoke.spec.ts`) with no `DMS_SMOKE_PORT` set
**When** a known value is written to `localStorage` in the first window and the app is then quit and relaunched
**Then** on relaunch the same origin is loaded and the previously-written `localStorage` value is still present — proving the origin (and therefore the storage partition) is stable across launches

**Given** an auth/session cookie has been set for the app origin in the first launch
**When** the app is quit and relaunched
**Then** the cookie is still present on the same origin after relaunch, so a logged-in session persists rather than being wiped by a new random port

**Given** the existing Electron smoke spec (`electron-package-launch.smoke.spec.ts`)
**When** it runs alongside the new persistence spec
**Then** all pass unchanged — no pre-existing test regresses (the `DMS_SMOKE_PORT`-driven smoke path is unaffected by the fixed default)

## Epic 13: Critical Review

We have reviewed the code as we've created it but now that we are basically done I would like to do a critical review of what we've ended up with.

As a start, come up with a plan of what we need to review, including code structure, design patterns, performance, and potential areas for improvement.
Additionally, consider reviewing the following aspects:

- Tailwind usage. Ensure that Tailwind classes are used consistently and effectively, and that custom styles are minimized where possible.
- Code readability and maintainability including naming conventions, code organization, code clarity and terseness (avoiding overly complex or verbose code), and adherence to best practices
- Consistency in coding style and conventions
- Error handling and logging
- Security implications and vulnerabilities
- Test coverage and quality of tests
- Dependencies and third-party libraries usage
- Documentation and comments
- Opportunities for refactoring and optimization

Your recommendations should be written into /.github/epic-descriptions/epics-9999-99-99.md
